title: CEDAR: Controlled and Event-Driven Demand Forecasting via Residual Decomposition
abstract: arXiv:2608.25871v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Forecasting in large-scale e-commerce marketplaces is increasingly required to support planning: merchants need to evaluate sales outcomes under future action sequences such as budget schedules, rather than passively predicting what happens next. However, most existing time series forecasting (TSF) approaches remain inherently passive. Even when incorporating operational decisions as auxiliary covariates, they typically optimize for correlation-based extrapolation under historical policies. This design suffers from autoregressive inertia and conflates endogenous market evolution with decision-induced transitions, leading to policy-insensitive rollouts and unreliable counterfactual analysis. To bridge this gap, we propose CEDAR (Controlled and Event-Driven Demand forecasting via Action-aware Residual decomposition), a two-stage framework for robust decision-conditioned simulation. translated_title: CEDAR：通过残差分解实现受控与事件驱动的需求预测
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.25871v1 公告类型：新论文  摘要：在大规模电子商务市场中，预测日益需要支持规划：商家需要评估未来行动序列（如预算安排）下的销售结果，而非被动地预测接下来会发生什么。然而，现有的大多数时间序列预测（TSF）方法本质上是被动的。即使将运营决策作为辅助协变量纳入，它们通常也优化基于历史政策下的相关性外推。这种设计存在自回归惯性，并将内生市场演变与决策引发的转变混为一谈，导致对政策不敏感的推演和不可靠的反事实分析。为弥合这一差距，我们提出CEDAR（通过行动感知残差分解实现受控与事件驱动的需求预测），一个用于稳健决策条件模拟的两阶段框架。在第一阶段，一个行动交织变换器学习受控...
tldr: CEDAR通过两阶段残差分解框架，将行动感知与事件驱动结合，解决了现有时间序列预测在决策条件模拟中的被动性和政策不敏感问题，实现了稳健的反事实需求预测。
en_tdlr: CEDAR introduces a two-stage residual decomposition framework that integrates action-awareness and event-driven mechanisms to overcome passivity and policy insensitivity in existing time series forecasting, enabling robust counterfactual demand prediction.
